title: Build Live Products
author: Rohit Swerashi
_note: Single source of truth for chapter/lesson TITLES and order. Content lives in chapters/chNN.js. A lesson is 'live' only when its content exists in a chapter file, else 'soon'. Keep ids identical between this file and chapter keys. No em-dashes anywhere.

chapters.title: Start Here
chapters.through_line: This is a build log, not a syllabus. You finish with a live product in users' hands, and you earn the right to build at every gate.

chapters.title: Understanding the Problem and the Customer
chapters.through_line: You don't have an idea, you have a problem hypothesis. Find the bleeding, expensive, frequent problem before you fall in love with a solution.

lessons.t: Where Problems Come From: Sourcing a Problem Worth Your Year
Defined vs Undefined: Two Ways Into a Build
Talk to Humans: Intent, Pain, and the Mom Test

chapters.title: Ideation and Picking the Wedge
chapters.through_line: The winning idea is the narrowest wedge that solves one painful problem so well that one specific person pays today.

lessons.t: Kill Your Favorite Idea (pain x reach x willingness to pay)

chapters.title: Validation: Will They Actually Pay
chapters.through_line: Validation is evidence of demand before you write code: a signup, a pre-payment, a signed pilot. 'I would use that' is politeness, not validation.

chapters.title: Feasibility, Pricing and Unit Economics
chapters.through_line: Easy to build is not the same as worth building. Before you scope anything, prove the ROI works and that someone will actually pay.

lessons.t: Is It Even Buildable? Team, Budget, Tech
Unit Economics: Will the Math Work?
Pricing and ROI: The Real Will-They-Pay Test

chapters.title: Positioning and Differentiation
chapters.through_line: If you cannot say in one sentence who it is for and why it beats the status quo, you have a feature, not a product.

lessons.t: Pick Your Enemy: Position Against the Status Quo
Beating the Three Objections (open source, build it themselves, why you)

chapters.title: Planning the Build
chapters.through_line: Clarity on the destination comes before the route. Define the ultimate goal, break it to functions and features, and sequence the milestones.

lessons.t: Define the Ultimate Goal and Outcome
Break to Unit Level and Set Milestones

chapters.title: Documentation: PRD and User Journey
chapters.through_line: A one-page spec that names the user, the core flow, the non-goals, and the done-bar beats a 30-page document nobody reads.

chapters.title: Prototyping: Fake It Before You Build It
chapters.through_line: A prototype's only job is to make a stranger's reaction cheap to collect. Deliver the outcome by hand before you write production code.

lessons.t: Clickable Prototypes That Get Honest Reactions

chapters.title: The MVP: The Boring V1
chapters.through_line: The MVP is the smallest thing that delivers the core value once, end to end, for real. It will look nothing like the version you imagined, and that is fine.

lessons.t: Prototype vs MVP vs Full Product
What Is In, What Is Out
The Critical Path: One Job, End to End

chapters.title: Building With AI
chapters.through_line: AI does not build the product for you. You break the plan to unit level and direct the coding agent precisely, or you get a demo, not an MVP.

lessons.t: Build With AI: PRD, Docs, and Decisions
Prompting Like a Builder: Break It to Unit Level
UI and UX With AI: References and Plain-English Translation
Vibe-Coding for Prototypes, Coding Agents for MVPs
The Product Levels: UI to Backend to Deploy to QA

chapters.title: Execution: Ship It Live
chapters.through_line: Shipping is a skill, not an event. Pick the boring stack, build the critical path first, and get live fast enough to still be wrong cheaply.

lessons.t: Build Level by Level, Never One-Shot
Get It Live: Deploy and Your First Non-Friend User

chapters.title: Analytics: Instrument and Read the Truth
chapters.through_line: Vanity metrics flatter you. Instrument the activation-to-retention funnel so the product tells you the truth about whether anyone got the value.

lessons.t: Pick Your North-Star and the Funnel

chapters.title: A/B Testing and Iteration
chapters.through_line: Once there is traffic, opinions lose. Run one disciplined experiment against one metric, and let the data decide: persevere, pivot, or kill.

lessons.t: A/B Testing at Low Traffic (and the alternatives)

chapters.title: Launch and Grow Toward Retention
chapters.through_line: A launch is a distribution plan, not an announcement. Earn one channel where your customer already gathers, fix the leaky funnel, then pour fuel.

lessons.t: A Launch Is a Distribution Plan
Fix the Leaky Funnel Before You Scale

chapters.title: The Build Lab: 10 Real 0 to 1 Teardowns
chapters.through_line: Every framework here is theory until you watch a real 2025 to 2026 product run it from zero to live. Reverse-engineer ten, then run the loop on your own bet.

lessons.t: Capstone: The Pivot, and Your Turn
